findings.text: blocking: §9's second done-when clause — "the deployed tools rerank with that measured gain reproduced on the same queries" — is not demonstrated. The pool sweep calls the production rerank_candidates over the 18 questions, but pool_sweep.py never measures the embedding-order (pre-rerank) nDCG@10/MRR: it records only the reranked order's metrics, and sweep.json carries no baseline field (recomputed here from sweep.json: pool 30 nDCG@10 0.3671, labelled-only 0.4637, recall@10 0.3750). The fragment's table therefore shows a reranked score with nothing to compare it against, and the reported 0.3671 at pool 30 does not reconcile with the prototype's 0.509 rerank figure — the label set differs (four census answers added, unlabelled candidates counted irrelevant), which changes IDCG, yet the fragment states neither the embedding baseline under its own labels nor why 0.3671 is not the reproduced 0.509. A reader cannot see the gain reproduced through the deployed path.

follow-on (spec floor not met, for coordinator adjudication): §9 requires "The rerank scores a pool larger than the 30 it returns" and sizes it "for example 100 or 150" to reach the census answers at ranks 159 to 181; the deployed RERANK_POOL is 30 (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:65), so the rerank still scores only "the top 30 alone" that §9 says "cannot reach either" census answer. The node's evidence picks 30 on whole-set nDCG@10, which the same caption admits penalises a deeper pool for its unlabelled tail, while the two metrics that do not carry that penalty both favour depth — labelled-only nDCG@10 rises 0.4637→0.6285 and recall@10 rises 0.3750→0.4956 from pool 30 to 150. The choice is documented and the budget constraint (p95 6.27 s at pool 100 against a 5 s budget) is real, but the spec's stated pool size is not met and the census answers remain out of reach.

follow-on: the gate logs in the reviewed run's reports tree carry no header naming the revision, tree and command they ran at (gate.log starts at the pytest session banner), so the cited result cannot be tied to a revision from the log alone — the same follow-on the docs-score-ties review recorded. The fragment's provenance comment does name the absolute reports directory, which lets a reader locate the scripts.

justifications.durability: seven committed, mechanism-stated commits and a committed evidence fragment plus figure; the pool constant's basis is stated in code and fragment. Docked because the measurement scripts and raw artifacts the claim rests on (pool_sweep.py, sweep.json, sweep_calls.json, table.py, plot_pool.py) live outside version control in the crew reports tree and only the fragment's provenance comment names their directory, and because the gate logs carry no revision header.
justifications.evidence: the fragment's pool table reproduces exactly from sweep.json (0.3671/0.2775/0.2872/0.2343 whole-set and 0.4637/0.4493/0.5673/0.6285 labelled-only, recomputed here), the negative control reproduces (identity rerank makes test_docs_report_follows_the_rerank_order fail on its ordering assertion, EXIT=1), and the scoped gate passes at 180 passed, 8 skipped, EXIT=0. Docked because the sweep has no embedding-order arm, so the headline comparison — the rerank's gain on the same queries through the deployed tools — is not measured, and the pool decision rests on the one metric the caption says is penalised by construction.
justifications.fit: the evidence lives at docs/evidence/fragments/discovery-judgments-through-jev/search-rerank.html and the figure at docs/figures/discovery-judgments-through-jev/search-rerank/pool_sweep.svg, the figure uses the project-absolute src /imas-codex/figures/..., the fragment carries one data-ink figure, and the shared core sits beside decide_batch in discovery/base (not in the search package), which a test asserts by parsing its imports.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deploy shape and the ranking-is-not-a-gate fallback are delivered exactly, and the judge-and-apply core is the single loop §9 asks for, but two spec points are not met: the pool is 30 rather than a pool larger than the 30 it returns, and the done-when's reproduced-gain clause is unmeasured.
justifications.reuse: rerank_candidates is a thin caller over the shared rerank_pool/decide_batch built in the same node, both callers reuse the discovery-relevance seat rather than adding one, find_code reuses the same core so the two code paths agree, and acall_decisions is reused through decide_batch. The only mild duplication is the locator extraction, which the sweep's own harness repeats.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff touches exactly the declared write paths (two source modules, three test files, the fragment, the figure); no repository file outside them, no plan HTML edit, no graph write, and every worktree commit is conventional with a body.
